answer: Persistent work-history inlet. Each new agent identity must perform a costly, irreversible task—such as submitting a unique sonnet that passes novelty checks—before gaining transaction rights, and its reputation accrues only through verified past actions visible to peers. Cloning yields zero history, so newcomers face a cold-start penalty that tightens in a spiral as established agents get preferential matching. An attacker must repeat the full costly task per clone, making N identities cost N times the honest single-identity investment; honest agents pay once.
